catalogue.title: Catalogue
catalogue.settingsHint: The use cases organizations are onboarded onto, and the kinds of thing the map is made of.
catalogue.subtitle: Two short lists the map is built out of: the use cases an organization is onboarded onto, and the kinds of thing a node can be.
catalogue.whyEditable: This screen can add and delete; Settings › Vocabulary deliberately cannot. Vocabulary is frozen because an item's status key is written into the append-only update thread, so merging two options would silently rewrite finished work with no undo. Nothing here is stored that way — a use case is referenced by a real foreign key — so add and delete are safe, and the database refuses the one delete that would lose something.
catalogue.hideVsDelete: Hiding is not deleting. A hidden use case leaves the pickers; every organization already recorded against it keeps it, and still shows it.
catalogue.notInstalled: The catalogue tables aren't in this project yet. Apply migrations 0023 and 0024, then reload.
catalogue.errSave: Couldn't save that. Nothing was changed.
catalogue.usageUnknown: Couldn't count what uses these, so the warnings below are missing. The database still refuses a delete that would lose data.
catalogue.nameArHint: Leave it empty and readers see the English name. Nothing breaks — it just stays untranslated.
catalogue.errNameLong: That name is too long. The limit is {max}.
catalogue.discardBody: The edits in this row haven't been saved.
catalogue.useCasesHint: The HL7/FHIR use cases an organization integrates. A version is its own row — “Medication Prescribe V2” sits beside V1 rather than replacing it.
catalogue.useCasesOrderNote: The order below is the one the catalogue was seeded in, and every screen reads it. It can't be changed from here yet.
catalogue.useCasesEmptyHint: Add the first one and it appears wherever an organization is scored.

arabicPending.one: 1 use case still has no Arabic name. This screen is where you add it.
arabicPending.other: {count} use cases still have no Arabic name. This screen is where you add them.

catalogue.needsArabicHint: The ten seeded use cases shipped with the Arabic name blank on purpose. An empty field here is a job to do, not a fault.
catalogue.inUseBlocks: Organizations are recorded against this, so the database refuses to delete it — that work would go with it. Hide it instead: it leaves the pickers and keeps its history.
catalogue.deleteUseCaseBody: No organization is recorded against it, so nothing is lost. If you only want it out of the pickers, hide it instead.
catalogue.addUseCaseHint: Name it the way the room says it. A version is a separate row, so write the version into the name.
catalogue.kindsHint: What a node on the map IS — a programme, a phase, an organization. Nothing in the app behaves differently because of a kind; it names the thing and orders the list.
catalogue.kindsNoHide: Kinds can't be hidden — the table has no such state. Delete one and the nodes that used it simply lose their kind; they stay on the map.
catalogue.kindsEmptyHint: Add one and it becomes selectable wherever a node is created.

kindUsage.one: 1 node on the map uses this
kindUsage.other: {count} nodes on the map use this

catalogue.deleteKindBody: The nodes that used this kind stay on the map and lose their kind. Nothing else changes.
catalogue.addKindHint: A colour is not asked for: colour on this map means track, at every depth.
catalogue.stagesHint: How far an organization has got — the rungs an account manager moves it up, from the first conversation to live. Position is the meaning here: a goal written as “at Testing/UAT or beyond” counts every rung from Testing/UAT downwards in this list.
catalogue.stagesOrderNote: Reordering this ladder restates every goal written as a count. “40 organizations at Go-live ready or beyond” is measured by a rung's position, so moving one changes which organizations count towards commitments nobody edited — and no goal records that it changed.
catalogue.stagesEmptyHint: Nobody can record where an organization got to until this ladder has rungs. Add the first one above — or, if migration 0026 has not been applied to this project yet, apply it and reload.
catalogue.stagesLoadFailed: Couldn't load the stage ladder. The two lists above are unaffected.

stagesArabicPending.one: 1 rung still has no Arabic name. This screen is where you add it.
stagesArabicPending.other: {count} rungs still have no Arabic name. This screen is where you add them.

catalogue.stagesNoThresholds: No rung has an expected length, so nothing anywhere in the app is counted as stalled. Open a rung and set one to turn that on.
catalogue.terminalHint: An organization on this rung has finished. Every live count in the app is the number of organizations on a rung marked this way, never a rung that happens to be named Live — so more than one rung may carry it, and nothing here asks how many do.
catalogue.pausedHint: Time spent on this rung counts against no threshold, so “blocked on the customer since March” stays a fact somebody recorded rather than an alarm the app raises every morning.
catalogue.expectedDaysHint: How long an organization may sit on this rung before it counts as stalled. Leave it empty and this rung has no threshold — nothing standing here is ever flagged. A whole number from 1 to {max}.
catalogue.errExpectedDays: The expected length has to be a whole number from 1 to {max}, or empty for no threshold.
catalogue.reorderStagesBody: Every goal written as a count is measured by a rung's position in this list: “40 organizations at Go-live ready or beyond by 31 December” counts everything from that rung downwards. Moving a rung changes which organizations meet commitments nobody edited, retroactively, and no goal records that it happened. Asked once a visit.
catalogue.deleteStageBody: The rung goes and nothing filed under it is deleted: the organizations standing on it stop showing a stage, and every goal that named it falls back to meaning “a terminal stage”, which is a different promise. Hiding it takes it out of the pickers and leaves everyone where they are.
catalogue.stageUsageUnknown: Couldn't count what sits at this stage or what refers to it, so this box can't say what the delete touches.
catalogue.addStageHint: It joins the end of the ladder. Move it into place afterwards — and read the note above the list before you do.
catalogue.laddersTitle: Which rungs each use case passes through
catalogue.laddersDesc: The five rungs are the programme's own and are not renamed here — Intake, DEV, STG/TEST, COC and PROD mean the same thing for every use case, or "how many are past DEV" stops having an answer. What changes below is which stops a use case actually makes.
catalogue.laddersUnconfigured: No ladder has been narrowed yet, so every use case passes through all five. Switch off the stops a use case does not make.
catalogue.laddersAlways: Intake and PROD are on every ladder. Every pair starts at Intake, and a ladder with no PROD is one nothing can finish. A use case that does not apply to a hospital is marked not applicable on that hospital instead.
